content.text: The description is repetitive and overstates some claims about the old checks. I’ll shorten the title and body around the enforced glibc minimum, musl fallback, and compatibility policy.

input.input:
text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/mise-pr-13296-body.md <<'EOF'
Linux GNU release builds now check for a maximum required glibc version of 2.18 across x86_64, aarch64, and armv7. This matches the requirement reported for the published v2026.9.10 binaries and catches increases introduced by future toolchain or dependency updates.

Previously, the checks allowed glibc 2.26 on x86_64 and 2.34 on aarch64, and did not cover armv7. A shared `GLIBC_FLOOR` makes the compatibility requirement explicit for all three targets.

The installation docs state the minimum and explain how to install a static musl build on systems with older glibc:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://mise.run | MISE_INSTALL_MUSL=1 sh
```

The installer detects musl systems automatically, but does not check the glibc version, so older glibc systems need this override.

The docs also describe the policy for future increases: distributions below a proposed minimum must have reached the end of standard vendor support. Extended-support programs do not delay an increase. The distribution lifecycle table provides context for that policy; it does not announce a planned increase.

Amazon Linux 2 is removed from the yum heading. Its glibc 2.26 still meets the documented minimum of 2.18.

## Validation

The existing validation reports that all three published GNU binaries pass the 2.18 check and fail at 2.17, that the target pattern includes all three GNU targets and excludes musl, macOS, and Windows, and that the changed files pass the scoped hk checks.

Related: #13295 adds a separate libstdc++ compatibility check.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5; version: 2.1.236.*

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/unavailable; version: unavailable.*
EOF
